title: E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
layout_note: A 2x2 commutative square: input graph top-left, its rotated copy top-right, the network's outputs for both in the bottom row; horizontal arrows are the transformation, vertical arrows the network.
grouping: No containers or panel letters; four drawings tied by four arrows. Two colour families mark input vs output: the top row has blue feature bars and salmon velocity arrows, the bottom row red feature bars and teal velocity arrows.
shapes_depth: A four-node toy graph: sage-green filled circles with thick black outlines and bold math labels (x1..x4), joined by plain black edges. Each node carries a tiny three-bar chart on a baseline (its features, labelled h1..h4) and a dashed coloured arrow (its vector, labelled v1..v4). Horizontal arrows are labelled S_g and T_g with a small dashed rotation glyph above; vertical arrows are labelled with a large italic phi.
proposed_highlight: No module box; the network is the single symbol on the vertical arrows. The point is carried by comparison: the bar charts are identical across each row while the arrows turn with the graph.
lesson: Attach each node's invariant features as a tiny bar chart and its vector as a dashed arrow, and swap the two colours between the input and output rows, so a reader sees the bars stay fixed under rotation while the arrows rotate with the graph.
notes: Venue from the PDF footer ('Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning'; venue_source: pdf); year 2021 = the ICML 2021 edition.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: E(n)-equivariant learning on graphs / point sets

insights.structure: Four copies of the same four-node graph form an unframed 2x2 commutative square: input top-left, rotated input top-right, network outputs for each directly beneath.
insights.data: Each node is a sage-green circle labelled x1..x4 carrying a tiny three-bar chart (invariant features h_i) and a dashed coloured arrow (vector v_i); the input row uses blue bars and salmon arrows, the output row red bars and teal arrows.
insights.emphasis: There is no network box at all: the method is the single italic phi on the two vertical arrows, and the claim is made by the bars staying identical across each row while the arrows rotate with the graph.
insights.flow: Horizontal arrows labelled S_g (top) and T_g (bottom) with a small dashed rotation glyph carry the transformation left-to-right; vertical phi arrows carry the network top-to-bottom, so the reader checks both paths around the square agree.
insights.avoid: The colour swap between rows (blue/salmon to red/teal) is never keyed in the figure, so a reader cannot tell it means 'output' rather than a different quantity.

arrangement.units: four unframed graph drawings in a 2x2 grid tied only by four labelled arrows; no frames or panel letters
arrangement.inputs_as: toy node-link graph with per-node bar charts and dashed vector arrows
arrangement.shared: the same network phi on both vertical arrows
